name: Ket
notes: Cyrillic-based practical orthography for Ket following Vajda (2004), Ket, and Vajda & Zinn's teaching materials. Ket has phonemic vowel length (doubled-vowel digraphs aa/ii/ee/oo/yy/oeoe mark long vowels, each earning its key by NOT being the concatenation of two short-vowel candidates) and lexical tone, which the orthography does not mark at all (Vajda 2004) -- the `stress` field is left unset and this is a documented exemption, not an oversight: Ket 'stress' is realised through the (unwritten) tonal system rather than a predictable stress rule. Ket also has a productive palatalised consonant series (dʲ lʲ nʲ sʲ tʲ), spelled with a following Cyrillic soft sign the same way Russian marks softness; per the ru ⟨бь⟩ precedent (AGENTS.md) this is a diacritic the soft-sign grapheme (mapped here to a silent empty candidate) already exists to compose, not a fact that earns Cyrillic+ь its own multigraph key, so the palatalised series is left as a documented, unencoded gap (as evn/Evenki documents the analogous native-only palatalization pattern) rather than enumerated as five extra keys. g is used for the velar stop /k̟/ (Ket has no phonemic voiced velar stop, per Vajda 2004); the plain non-palatalised lateral is velarised /lˠ/; short /u/ is realised [ʊ] (Vajda 2004), contrasting with long /uː/ spelled уу.
